nodes.label: Operator
nodes.description: The developer/orchestrator running es-view in the browser. Here they open a sticky's Detail panel, click 'view source' under an anchor to pull the real code inline, and/or click the anchor link to deep-link the file into VS Code.

nodes.label: ViewSource
nodes.description: Pull the real source code behind a model anchor and show it inline in the Detail panel. The operator clicks the 'view source' toggle on an anchor; the SPA asks the server for a line-windowed excerpt of the file at the anchor's repo-relative path.

tactical.explanation: The Anchor component's toggle() (Detail.jsx) lazily calls fetchSource(a.path, a.line) (api.js), which issues GET /api/source?path&line&ctx. The server handler (server.ts, createServer) reads the query params, 400s if `path` is missing, coerces line/ctx with Number()||undefined, and delegates to viewSource(sourceGateway, resolved.repoRoot, relPath, line, ctx) (the application query), which calls through to the fs source-gateway's readSource. The command carries no write; it is a synchronous read whose result the panel renders. A closed toggle re-clicks to hide (src state null=closed).

anchors.note: lazy toggle: fetchSource(a.path, a.line) on first open
GET /api/source handler: parse params, 400 if no path, call viewSource

nodes.label: Source Reader (repo-root sandbox)
nodes.description: The consistency boundary around reading real code behind an anchor: every source read must stay inside the resolved repo root. Stateless (its 'state' is the repo working tree on disk, reached through node:fs); recovered as an aggregate because it owns the path-traversal invariant and returns the source excerpt. MED confidence — it is a guarded read helper, arguably infra rather than a domain aggregate.

tactical.explanation: readSource(repoRoot, relPath, line, ctx) (fs source-gateway adapter) resolves relPath against path.resolve(repoRoot) via the pure guardPath() helper, enforces the sandbox guard, and on success reads the file with fs.readFileSync, splits on /\r?\n/, clamps the requested line into range via the pure lineWindow() helper, and returns a { path, exists, line, startLine, endLine, code } window (ctx lines above/below, default 8). The guard + window math now live in domain/source/source-window.ts (pure, no fs); the fs read itself lives in the adapter. repoRoot comes from resolveModel: explicit --repo-root > packageRoot (bundled-example self-model) > model.meta.repoRoot > cwd.

anchors.note: sandboxed read owner: resolve, guard, read, window
handler returns viewSource(sourceGateway, resolved.repoRoot, ...) as the /api/source body
how resolvedRepoRoot (the sandbox root) is chosen

nodes.label: Source reads stay inside the repo root
nodes.description: A source read may only resolve to a file at or under the repo root; a path that escapes it is REJECTED. ERROR-level (rejects the read): the request returns { exists:false, error:'path escapes repo root' } and no file is read. Effective against classic ../ traversal and absolute-path injection (see notes), but it is a lexical guard only — it does not resolve symlinks and does not restrict reads to files that are actually model anchors (see hot-source-read-scope).

tactical.explanation: root = path.resolve(repoRoot); abs = path.resolve(root, relPath) (which normalizes any ../ sequences and lets an absolute relPath override root). The guard rejects unless abs === root OR abs starts with root + path.sep — the trailing separator blocks sibling-prefix escapes (e.g. /repo-secrets vs /repo). URL-encoded traversal (%2e%2e%2f) is decoded by URLSearchParams before path.resolve normalizes it, so encoded ../ is also caught. After the guard, a missing/non-file path returns { exists:false, error:'not found' }. The guard itself is now the pure guardPath() function in domain/source/source-window.ts; the fs source-gateway adapter calls it before reading.

anchors.note: guard: abs !== root && !abs.startsWith(root + path.sep) => 'path escapes repo root'

nodes.label: Source excerpt
nodes.description: The line-windowed slice of real code the Detail panel shows inline under an anchor: a { path, exists, line, startLine, endLine, code } window (or an error note when the file is missing or the path escaped). This is the grounding a human reads next to the recovered sticky, and the same anchor block also offers the VS Code deep link.

tactical.explanation:
Built by readSource: it slices lines[startLine-1 .. endLine] around the clamped anchor line (ctx=8 default, computed by the pure lineWindow() helper) and joins them into `code`. server.ts returns the object verbatim as the /api/source JSON body. The Anchor component renders it: while loading a 'loading…' note, then either 
{src.code}
on exists, or a 'source not found at repo root ()' note otherwise.

anchors.note: return { path, exists, line, startLine, endLine, code } window
render: <pre class=src-code> excerpt, or 'source not found' note

fields.name: code
fields.derivation: The file's text sliced to a window of ctx lines above/below the anchor line (default 8), i.e. lines[startLine-1 .. endLine] joined with newlines. Empty/omitted when the file is missing or the path escaped the repo root.

sources.note: read whole file, keep only the [startLine, endLine] line window

fields.name: startLine / endLine
fields.derivation: The clamped excerpt window: ln = clamp(line||1, 1, fileLength); startLine = max(1, ln-ctx); endLine = min(fileLength, ln+ctx). Guarantees an in-range window even for a rotted/overshooting anchor line.

evidence.note: Math.max/Math.min clamping of line into range

nodes.label: Repo working tree (sandbox root)
nodes.description: The checked-out repository rooted at resolvedRepoRoot, reached through node:fs. It is the sandbox boundary for /api/source: readSource may read any file at or under this root. Read-only on this flow (fs.readFileSync); no writes.

tactical.explanation: resolvedRepoRoot is chosen by resolveModel (explicit --repo-root > packageRoot for the bundled self-model > model.meta.repoRoot > cwd) and passed as readSource's repoRoot. path.resolve(repoRoot) is the guard's `root`, computed in the pure guardPath() helper.

anchors.note: root = path.resolve(repoRoot) — the filesystem sandbox root

nodes.label: Source file at anchor path
nodes.description: An arbitrary file addressed by a model anchor's repo-relative path (e.g. src/domain/model/merge.ts), read at or under the repo root. The excerpt projects a line window of this file. Note the read is NOT limited to files that are actually model anchors — any file under the root is reachable (see hot-source-read-scope).

tactical.explanation: abs = path.resolve(root, relPath); after the sandbox guard (guardPath) passes and fs.statSync(abs).isFile() is true, fs.readFileSync(abs,'utf8') loads the whole file, split into lines for windowing.

nodes.label: VS Code
nodes.description: The local VS Code editor, reached through the OS handler for the vscode:// URL scheme. Clicking an anchor's link deep-links the exact file and line open in the editor — an out-of-band escape hatch from the inline excerpt to the full file in an IDE.

tactical.explanation: anchorUrl(repoRoot, a) builds `vscode://file/<repoRoot>/<a.path>:<line>`; the Anchor component renders it as the <a class='anchor' href={anchorUrl(...)}> link text of every anchor. The browser/OS resolves the vscode:// scheme and hands off to the editor; the app has no further involvement.

flows.name: Operator pulls the real code behind an anchor
flows.summary: From a sticky's Detail panel, each tactical anchor offers two ways into the real code: a 'view source' toggle that pulls a line-windowed excerpt inline, and a vscode://file link that opens the exact file+line in VS Code. The inline path calls GET /api/source, which reads the file through a repo-root-sandboxed helper (readSource) whose path-traversal guard rejects any path that escapes the repo root, then returns a clamped window of lines around the anchor. The point is to ground a recovered, inferred sticky in verifiable source without leaving the explorer, and to hand off to a real editor when the operator wants the whole file.
flows.trigger: Operator clicks 'view source' under an anchor in the Detail panel (or clicks the anchor's vscode:// link).

hotspots.label: /api/source can read any file under the repo root, not just model anchors
hotspots.description: The path-traversal guard correctly blocks ../ and absolute-path escapes, but it only sandboxes reads to the repo ROOT — it does not restrict them to files that are actually anchors in the model, and it is a lexical guard that does NOT resolve symlinks. So the endpoint will serve the contents of ANY file under the repo root (e.g. .env, .git/config, committed keys) to whoever can reach the server, and a symlink inside the tree pointing outside would be followed. The default bind is 127.0.0.1 (localhost only, no auth), but --host accepts any address (e.g. 0.0.0.0), which would expose this unauthenticated file-read on the network. Human question: is arbitrary repo-root file read the intended trust boundary, and should the guard additionally (a) restrict to known anchor paths, (b) realpath-resolve symlinks, and/or (c) refuse to bind a non-loopback --host without auth?

tactical.explanation: guardPath guards abs against root+path.sep (domain/source/source-window.ts) — lexically sound, but there is no allowlist of anchor paths and no fs.realpath check, and the read (fs.readFileSync in the fs source-gateway) will return any in-root file. The handler is unauthenticated (server.ts's /api/source branch). startServer defaults host to 127.0.0.1 (server.ts) but the CLI's --host option (cli.ts, on the `view` subcommand) overrides it with no auth gate, so 0.0.0.0 would publish the read to the LAN.

anchors.note: lexical sandbox guard: no anchor allowlist, no symlink realpath
--host option on the `view` subcommand overrides the loopback default with no auth
